srcline: Sourced reporting · RID, MEA, airport notices · asset list from public references
chartSub: Outages, dam releases, disruptions and damage by month.
status: A reference map plus a thin event record. 26 key assets (airports, ports, dams, border bridges, power, water) and 15 events for Jan–Sep 2026. Unplanned blackouts, water failures and port disruptions are missing because their pages could not be opened.

assets.title: Suvarnabhumi Airport (BKK)
assets.detail: Thailand's primary international airport serving Bangkok, operated by Airports of Thailand.

assets.title: Don Mueang International Airport (DMK)
assets.detail: Bangkok's second airport and main low-cost carrier hub, operated by Airports of Thailand.

assets.title: Phuket International Airport (HKT)
assets.detail: Main gateway for Phuket and the Andaman coast; described by Wikipedia as one of Thailand's busiest airports.

assets.title: Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX)
assets.detail: Principal airport of northern Thailand, operated by Airports of Thailand.

assets.title: Hat Yai International Airport (HDY)
assets.place: Hat Yai International Airport, Khlong La
assets.detail: Main airport of the lower south, operated by Airports of Thailand.

assets.title: U-Tapao International Airport (UTP)
assets.detail: Public international airport serving Rayong and Pattaya; the civil terminal shares the site with a navy airfield (military facilities not mapped here).

assets.title: Mae Fah Luang–Chiang Rai International Airport (CEI)
assets.place: Mae Fah Luang–Chiang Rai International Airport, Ban Du
assets.detail: Airport serving Chiang Rai and Phayao, operated by Airports of Thailand.

assets.title: Laem Chabang Port
assets.detail: Thailand's largest container port, overseen by the Port Authority of Thailand.

assets.title: Bangkok Port (Khlong Toei)
assets.detail: River port on the Chao Phraya handling container and general cargo, limited to smaller vessels; operated by the Port Authority of Thailand.

assets.title: Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate and Port
assets.detail: Thailand's largest industrial estate and petrochemical hub, with a deep-sea industrial port; run by the Industrial Estate Authority of Thailand.

assets.title: Songkhla Port
assets.detail: Regional multipurpose deep-sea port on the Gulf of Thailand handling containers, general cargo and petroleum products.

assets.title: Ranong Port
assets.detail: Port Authority of Thailand port on the Kraburi River estuary facing Myanmar, Thailand's Andaman-side gateway.

assets.title: Mae Moh Power Plant
assets.detail: Thailand's largest lignite-fired power plant (per EGAT), fed by the adjacent Mae Moh mine.

assets.title: Bhumibol Dam
assets.detail: Concrete arch dam on the Ping River for hydropower, storage, flood control and irrigation; a key Chao Phraya basin reservoir.

assets.title: Sirikit Dam
assets.detail: Embankment dam on the Nan River for irrigation, flood control and hydropower; a key Chao Phraya basin reservoir.

assets.title: Srinagarind Dam
assets.detail: Embankment hydroelectric dam on the Khwae Yai River with pumped-storage units.

assets.title: Ubol Ratana Dam
assets.detail: Multi-purpose earth/rockfill dam on the Nam Phong for power, irrigation and flood control in the northeast.

assets.title: Pa Sak Jolasid Dam
assets.detail: Largest reservoir in central Thailand on the Pa Sak River, used for irrigation and flood control for the lower Chao Phraya basin.

assets.title: Mae Klong Dam
assets.detail: Barrage on the Mae Klong River supplying irrigation across six provinces and raw water for western Bangkok; run by RID and EGAT.

assets.title: First Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
assets.detail: Mekong road-and-rail bridge (opened 1994) linking Nong Khai with Vientiane.

assets.title: Second Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
assets.detail: Mekong road bridge (opened 2007) linking Mukdahan with Savannakhet on the East–West Economic Corridor.

assets.title: Third Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
assets.detail: Mekong bridge (opened 2011) linking Nakhon Phanom with Thakhek.

assets.title: Fourth Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
assets.detail: Mekong bridge (opened 2013) linking Chiang Khong with Houayxay.

assets.title: Fifth Thai–Lao Friendship Bridge
assets.detail: Mekong bridge (opened 2025 per Wikipedia) linking Bueng Kan with Pakxan.

assets.title: Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal
assets.place: Krung Thep Aphiwat Central Terminal (Bang Sue)
assets.detail: Thailand's largest railway station and main intercity rail hub, also serving SRT Red Lines and the MRT.

assets.title: Bangkhen Water Treatment Plant
assets.detail: Metropolitan Waterworks Authority's main plant treating Chao Phraya raw water for Bangkok (about 3.6 million m3/day per MWA).

notes: Assets are reference points, not events. Airports, ports, dams and bridges are shown as rings on the map and listed under Key assets. They are not in the Timeline and say nothing about current status.
Planned power cuts are scheduled maintenance. They are recorded because they disrupt service, not because anything failed.
Dam notices are claims. Chao Phraya Dam release warnings on 19–23 Sep describe one rising-flow episode, so the map shows several markers for one event.
Crashes are in other tabs. The Sikhio and Makkasan rail disasters are recorded in Transportation and Public safety and not repeated here.
The telecom record is weak. It rests on one automated connectivity measurement that its source rates as low corroboration.
